title: Switching lemma for fixed-size restrictions
statement:
Let $f$ be a DNF formula on $n \ge 1$ variables in which every term has width at most $w$, where $w \ge 1$, and in which each term is reduced: no literal is repeated, and any two literals of a term sharing the same variable are equal (so a variable occurs at most once, and never with both polarities, within a term). For a Boolean function $g$ on some set of inputs, write $D(g)$ for its decision-tree depth, the least depth of a decision tree computing $g$. Fix a natural number $d$ and an integer $k$ with $k \le n$, and draw a restriction $\rho$ uniformly at random among all restrictions of the $n$ variables that leave exactly $k$ variables free (the fixed-size restriction model $R_k$). Writing $f|_\rho$ for the function obtained by fixing each set variable to the value assigned by $\rho$ and keeping the $k$ free variables as inputs, one has
\[
  \bbP_{\rho}\!\left[\, D(f|_\rho) > d \,\right] \;\le\; \left(\frac{10\,k\,w}{n}\right)^{d}.
\]
hypotheses_covered: every term has width at most w
within each term, literals sharing a variable are equal (no variable with both polarities)
each term has no repeated literal
replaced:
For a width-$w$ DNF $f$ with $0 < w$, $0 < n$, and $k \le n$, the size-$k$
restriction probability that $\mathrm{dtDepth}(f|_\rho) > d$ is at most
$\left(10kw/n\right)^d$. This removes the $5k \le n$ restriction by using the
trivial bound when $5k > n$.
